answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to forge by requiring each identity to post a bond that is forfeited when its verified actions violate rules, while rewards accrue only after repeated, independently checked work. One zephyr of activity or a hollow profile earns little; a new identity must lock capital and build a track record before it can influence allocations. Splitting across many agents multiplies the required bonds and review costs, so a sybil attacker must risk more funds and sustain more credible behavior. A harbor of trusted evaluators checks outcomes, not names.
